choices.text: The ! substitutes an empty string, so Length is 0.
The ! only silenced the compiler; reading Length throws NullReferenceException at runtime.
The ! throws ArgumentNullException right at the assignment.
The compiler inserts a null check that skips the Length read.

choices: The ! substitutes an empty string, so Length is 0.
The ! only silenced the compiler; reading Length throws NullReferenceException at runtime.
The ! throws ArgumentNullException right at the assignment.
The compiler inserts a null check that skips the Length read.

items.explanation: ! does not change runtime behavior; if you're wrong you still get an NRE (15-nullable-reference-types.md:85).

items.prompt: Goal: predict deferred execution. `var evens = source.Where(n => n % 2 == 0);` is defined over `List<int> { 1, 2, 3 }`, then `source.Add(4)` runs, then `foreach (var n in evens) Console.Write(n);`. Which observation verifies you understood it?

choices.text: It throws InvalidOperationException because the source changed after the query was built.
It writes only 2, because Where snapshotted the list when the query was defined.
It writes 2 then 4: the filter runs at enumeration time against the list's current contents.
It writes nothing until ToList() is called on the query.

choices: It throws InvalidOperationException because the source changed after the query was built.
It writes only 2, because Where snapshotted the list when the query was defined.
It writes 2 then 4: the filter runs at enumeration time against the list's current contents.
It writes nothing until ToList() is called on the query.

items.explanation: A deferred query reflects the current state of the source when enumerated, not when defined (10-linq.md:225-231).

items.explanation: Bare throw; preserves the stack trace; throw ex; resets it (11-exceptions-and-resources.md:108-113).

items.prompt: Goal: change one field of a positional record. After `var older = p1 with { Age = 31 };` where p1.Age was 30, which observation verifies how `with` works?

choices.text: older and p1 are the same reference, so p1 == older is true.
older.Age is 31 and p1.Age is still 30: with makes a modified copy.
Compile error: positional properties are init-only, so Age can never be changed.
Both p1.Age and older.Age are 31, since with mutates the original through its init setter.

choices: older and p1 are the same reference, so p1 == older is true.

items.explanation: Non-destructive copy: the original is unchanged (07-structs-records-enums.md:104-107, 117).

items.prompt: Goal: know where an EF Core query stops being SQL. A query puts a custom C# method `MyComplexFormat(c)` inside `.Where(...)` before `ToListAsync()`. What does modern EF Core do?

choices.text: It silently pulls every row and filters in memory.
It translates the method body into a SQL function automatically.
It throws, because a Where it cannot translate is never run on the client.
It ignores the predicate and returns all rows.

choices: It silently pulls every row and filters in memory.
It translates the method body into a SQL function automatically.
It throws, because a Where it cannot translate is never run on the client.
It ignores the predicate and returns all rows.

items.explanation: Only the final Select may run on the client; an untranslatable Where/OrderBy always throws (19-entity-framework-core.md:236).

choices.text: Add .AsNoTracking() to the query.

items.explanation: For read-only queries disable tracking: faster, less memory (19-entity-framework-core.md:221-232).

items.prompt: Goal: predict EF Core behaviour. Customers are loaded with `await _db.Customers.ToListAsync()` (no Include, no lazy-loading proxies) and the loop prints `c.Orders.Count` for each. What happens?

choices.text: EF issues one extra query per customer, the classic N+1.
Every customer prints 0: Orders was never loaded, a silent wrong answer.
EF automatically joins Orders into the first query.
EF throws because the navigation was not Included.

choices: EF issues one extra query per customer, the classic N+1.
Every customer prints 0: Orders was never loaded, a silent wrong answer.
EF automatically joins Orders into the first query.
EF throws because the navigation was not Included.

items.explanation: Lazy loading is off unless proxies are installed; without it c.Orders is empty and prints 0 (19-entity-framework-core.md:204-207).
